en: Thus have I heard: Majjhima Nikāya 49, the Brahmanimantanika Sutta. Thus have I heard: [the Blessed One was once staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. ... [The discourse continues with the Buddha’s teaching on the four jhānas and the invitation of Brahmā Sahampati. ... [End of Majjhima Nikāya 49]
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!”
“Venerable Sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Once, bhikkhus, I was dwelling at Ukkaṭṭhā in the Subhaga Grove at the foot of a king of sāla trees.”
Now at that time, monks, such an evil speculative view had arisen in Baka the Brahmā:
"This is permanent, this is stable, this is eternal, this is absolute, this is not subject to passing away;
for this is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and does not reappear. And there is no other escape higher than this."
Then, monks, having known with my own mind the reflection that had arisen in the mind of Baka Brahmā—
just as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm— even so, vanishing from the Sāla-tree king’s foot in the Subhaga Grove at Ukkatthā,
I appeared in that Brahma-world. Monks, Baka Brahmā saw me coming from afar.
Having seen me, he said this to me:
"Come, dear sir! Welcome, dear sir!
It has been a long time, dear sir, since you last made the occasion to come here."
"For this, dear sir, is permanent; this is stable; this is eternal; this is absolute; this is subject to no change;
for this is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and does not reappear.
And there is no other escape beyond this."
When this was said, monks, I said this to Baka the Brahmā:
“Baka the Brahmā is indeed enveloped in ignorance! Baka the Brahmā is indeed enveloped in ignorance!
For he speaks of what is truly impermanent as permanent, and of what is truly unstable as stable.”
He will speak of what is actually non-eternal as being eternal; he will speak of what is incomplete as being complete;
he will speak of what is subject to falling away as being not subject to falling away;
and he will speak of that wherein one is born, ages, dies, falls away, and reappears.
“This indeed is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and does not reappear”;
yet, although there is another, higher escape, he will say, ‘There is no other, higher escape.
Then, monks, Māra the Evil One, having possessed a certain member of Brahmā’s retinue, said this to me:

“Monk, monk! Do not be afraid, do not be afraid! For this, monk, is Brahmā, the Great Brahmā, the Conqueror, the Unconquered, the All-Seeing, the All-Powerful, the Lord, the Maker, the Creator, the Chief, the Ordainer, the Father of all that has been and will be.
There were, monk, those ascetics and brahmins of the past in the world who censured the earth and loathed the earth.”
Those who revile water and loathe water; those who revile fire and loathe fire; those who revile wind and loathe wind;
those who revile spirits and loathe spirits; those who revile the gods and loathe the gods; those who revile Pajāpati and loathe Pajāpati;
those who revile Brahmā and loathe Brahmā.
With the breakup of the body, at the cutting off of life, they were established in an inferior body.
But as for those ascetics and brahmins whom you previously saw in the world praising earth and delighting in earth,
praising water and delighting in water, praising fire and delighting in fire, praising air and delighting in air—
Those who praise the spirits and rejoice in the spirits, who praise the gods and rejoice in the gods, who praise Pajāpati and rejoice in Pajāpati,
and who praise Brahmā and rejoice in Brahmā—
upon the dissolution of the body, at the cutting off of life, they are established in a refined body.
“Bhikkhu, I say this to you:
‘Come now, dear sir, do exactly as Brahmā tells you; do not overstep the word of Brahmā.
If you, bhikkhu, were to overstep the word of Brahmā, it would be just as if a man...”
"One might ward off approaching glory with a staff; or else, bhikkhu, it will happen to you just as if a man falling into the precipice of hell were to miss the earth with his hands and feet.
Come now, dear sir, do exactly what Brahmā tells you; do not overstep the word of Brahmā."
“Do you not see, bhikkhu, the assembly of Brahmās gathered together?
Thus, monks, did Māra the Evil One lead me toward the assembly of Brahmās.
When this was said, monks, I spoke thus to Māra the Evil One:
“I know you well, Evil One! Do not think:
‘He does not know me.
You are Māra, Evil One.”
Whatever Brahmā there is, Pāpima, whatever assembly of Brahmās, and whatever members of Brahmā’s retinue—all these are already in your hands, all are already under your control.
For it occurs to you, Pāpima, thus:
"May this one also be in my hands; may this one also be under my control."
"But as for me, Evil One, I have neither fallen into your hands nor come under your power.
When this was said, monks, Baka Brahmā said this to me:
"For I, dear sir, being permanent, say 'it is permanent'; being stable, say 'it is stable'."
I say that what is indeed eternal, I call "eternal"; what is indeed absolute, I call "absolute";
what is indeed subject to no decay, I call "subject to no decay.
And where one is neither born, nor ages, nor dies, nor passes away, nor reappears—that alone do I describe as such.
“For this is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and does not reappear.
And since there is no other higher escape, I say, “There is no other higher escape.
Monks, in the past there were ascetics and brahmins in the world who, for as long as your life-span was, engaged solely in ascetic practices.

They would know thus: if there were another, higher escape, they would know, "There is another, higher escape"; or if there were no other, higher escape, they would know, "There is no other, higher escape.
Regarding this, monk, I say to you:
"You will not see any other, higher escape; you will merely partake in weariness and frustration."
If you, monk, should cling to earth, you will be one who dwells in my vicinity, dwelling in my domain, to be dealt with according to my will, and to be cast out.
If [you should cling] to water… to fire…
... the wind ...
the spirits ...
the gods ...
‘If you will cling to Pajāpati… or to Brahmā, you will be one who dwells near me, one who dwells within my domain, to be dealt with as I wish,
and one to be cast out. ‘I too, Brahmā, know this:’
“If I should cling to earth, I would be one who dwells near it, one who dwells within its substance; I would be subject to being done with at will and liable to be cast out.
If [I should cling] to water… to fire…”
... the wind ...
the spirits ...
the gods ...

“I shall cling to Pajāpati… I shall cling to Brahmā; I will be your attendant, your bedfellow, one who may be treated as you wish and cast out at will. Nevertheless, O Brahmā, I understand your range and I understand your power:
“Such is the great psychic power of Baka Brahmā, such is the great majesty of Baka Brahmā, such is the great authority of Baka Brahmā.”
"But how, dear sir, do you know my destination and know my power, such that you say:
'The Brahmā Baka is so mighty in psychic power, the Brahmā Baka is so great in majesty, the Brahmā Baka is so influential'?
"As far as the moon and sun..."
They avoid [the world], shining resplendently in all directions;
for as far as a thousandfold world-system extends,
there your power prevails.
You know both the higher and the lower,
as well as those with passion and those free from passion;
you know existence in this state and existence in another state.
"The coming and going of beings.
Thus, Brahmā, I understand your destination and I understand your power:
"Baka the Brahmā is so mighty, Baka the Brahmā is so powerful, Baka the Brahmā is so influential."
"There is, Brahmā, another body that you do not know and do not see,
but which I know and see.
There is, Brahmā, a body called 'Radiant' (Ābhassara), from which you have passed away and been reborn here."
Because you have lived here for too long, that mindfulness has been forgotten by you; therefore, you neither know nor see it, whereas I both know and see it.
Even so, Brahmā, I am not your equal in direct knowledge, let alone inferior.
But I am indeed superior to you.
There is, Brahmā, a body called Subhakiṇha, a body called Vehapphala, and a body called Abhibhū; these you neither know nor see, but I both know and see them.
"Even so, Brahmā, I am not your equal in direct knowledge; how could I be inferior?
On the contrary, I am indeed superior to you.
For I, Brahmā, having directly known the earth as earth, [know] that which has not been experienced by the earth in its state as earth."
Having directly known that, Brahmā, I did not exist as earth, I did not exist apart from earth, I did not exist from earth, I did not think "earth is mine," and I did not address earth.
Even so, Brahmā, I am not your equal in direct knowledge; how then could there be inferiority?
But I am even greater than you.
As for water, Brahmā...
[and so on] ...as for fire, Brahmā... [and so on].
"Brahmā, I [have known] the wind...
Brahmā, I [have known] beings...
Brahmā, I [have known] the devas..."
"Brahmā, I [have seen] Pajāpati... Brahmā...
and the Ābhassara devas, Brahmā..."
“Brahmā, I have [dwelt] in the Subhakiṇha realm...
I have [dwelt] in the Vehapphala realm...
I have [dwelt] as an Abhibhū, Brahmā...”
“Brahmā, having directly known everything from every perspective—whatever has not been experienced by everything in its entirety as everything—I did not claim to have direct knowledge of that;
I did not exist in everything, I did not exist from everything, I did not think ‘everything is mine,’ and I did not assert ‘everything.
Even so, Brahmā, I am not your equal in direct knowledge, much less inferior.”
"Then indeed, I am even more so than you.
"If, dear sir, there is something that has not been experienced by anyone as anything, then let it not be empty or void for you through higher knowledge.
Consciousness—non-manifesting, infinite, radiant on all sides—that has not been experienced by the earth as the quality of earth..."
It has not been experienced as the watery nature of water; it has not been experienced as the fiery nature of fire; it has not been experienced as the windy nature of wind;
it has not been experienced as the elemental nature of the elements; it has not been experienced as the divine nature of the gods; it has not been experienced as the lordly nature of Pajāpati;
it has not been experienced as the Brahma-nature of the Brahmas; it has not been experienced as the radiant nature of the Ābhassara deities.
‘What has not been experienced by the Subhakiṇha devas in their state as Subhakiṇhas, what has not been experienced by the Vehapphala devas in their state as Vehapphala,
what has not been experienced by Abhibhu in his state as Abhibhu, and what has not been experienced by Sabbu in his state as Sabbu—
come now, dear sir, watch while I vanish from you.’”
“Come now, Brahmā, disappear from my sight if you dare!
Then, monks, Baka the Brahmā thought,
“I shall vanish from the sight of the ascetic Gotama, I shall vanish from the sight of the ascetic Gotama,” yet he was unable to vanish from my sight.
When this was said, monks, I said to Baka Brahmā:
“Well then, Brahmā, let me disappear from you.
“Well then, dear sir, do you disappear from me if you dare,” he replied.
Then, monks, I performed such a feat of psychic power that Brahmā,
the assembly of Brahmā, and the retinue of Brahmā would hear my voice but not see me.
Having vanished, I spoke this verse:
“Having seen the fear in existence,
and having sought the end of existence,
I did not praise any form of existence whatsoever.”
"And they do not cling to delight.
Then, monks, Brahmā, the assembly of Brahmā, and the retinue of Brahmā were struck with a sense of wonder and amazement, thinking:
"How extraordinary, indeed! How marvelous, indeed!"

"The ascetic Gotama possesses great psychic power and great majesty; indeed, we have never before seen or heard of another ascetic or brahmin who possessed such great psychic power and such great majesty as this ascetic Gotama,
the son of the Sakyans, who went forth from the Sakyan clan."
“Alas, for this generation that delights in existence, that finds pleasure in existence, that rejoices in existence—you have uprooted existence by its very root!
Then, monks, Māra the Evil One, having possessed a certain member of the Brahmā’s retinue, said this to me:
“If indeed, dear sir, you understand thus, and if you have awakened to this truth, do not lead disciples away, do not lead those who have gone forth.”
Do not teach the Dhamma to disciples, do not [teach it] to those who have gone forth;
do not form attachments toward disciples, do not [form attachments] toward those who have gone forth.
Bhikkhu, in the past there were in the world ascetics and brahmins who claimed to be arahants, perfectly enlightened Buddhas.
They led those disciples who had gone forth; they taught the Dhamma to those disciples who had gone forth;

they felt attachment toward those disciples who had gone forth. Having led those disciples who had gone forth, having taught the Dhamma to those disciples who had gone forth, their minds became attached to those disciples who had gone forth.
With the breakup of the body, at the cutting off of life, they were established in an inferior state.
But as for those ascetics and brahmins in the world whom you previously claimed were Arahants and Perfectly Enlightened Ones—those did not lead on disciples or those gone forth;
they did not teach the Dhamma to disciples or to those gone forth.
They did not harbor attachment toward disciples nor toward those who had gone forth; they did not lead disciples away nor those who had gone forth;
they did not teach the Dhamma to disciples nor to those who had gone forth; they were not of minds attached to disciples nor to those who had gone forth.
With the breakup of the body, after the cutting off of life, they were established in a sublime body.
“Monk, I say this to you:
‘Come now, dear sir, dwell at ease, devoted to a pleasant abiding in this very life; for what is wholesome, dear sir, is not something to be proclaimed; do not advise others.
When this was said, monks, I said this to Māra the Evil One:”
“I do indeed know you, Evil One; do not think:
‘He does not know me.
You are Māra, Evil One.”
"You do not speak thus to me out of compassion for my welfare, Evil One;
you speak thus to me out of compassion for my harm, Evil One.
For it is this that occurs to you, Evil One:"
“Those to whom the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma will transcend my domain,” he thought.
Yet, O Evil One, while being non-Perfectly Enlightened Ones, they claimed, “We are Perfectly Enlightened Ones.
But I, O Evil One, being truly a Perfectly Enlightened One, claim, “I am a Perfectly Enlightened One.”
For whether the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma to his disciples, Evil One, he remains the same; and whether the Tathāgata does not teach the Dhamma to his disciples, Evil One, he remains the same.
For whether the Tathāgata leads his disciples along, Evil One, he remains the same; and whether the Tathāgata does not lead his disciples along, Evil One, he remains the same. And why is that?
“Māra, the taints of the Tathāgata that lead to defilement, to renewed existence, to distress, to the ripening of suffering, and to future birth, aging, and death—
these have been abandoned by him, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and are no longer subject to future arising. Just as, Māra,
a palm tree with its crown cut off is incapable of further growth, so it is with the Tathāgata.”

“In the same way, Evil One, whatever taints there are in the Tathāgata that lead to defilement, to renewed existence, that are vexatious and result in suffering, leading to future birth, aging, and death— those have been abandoned by him,
cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated so that they are no longer subject to future arising. Thus,
because of this refusal to converse with Māra and the invitation from Brahmā, this exposition is called “The Invitation of Brahmā.”
The Brahmanimantanika Sutta, the ninth, is finished.
